title: Preparing for your first meeting
summary: What to bring, what we will ask, and how the conflict check works.
body:
1. The contract or documents at the center of the issue
  2. A list of the people and companies involved (for the conflict check)
  3. Key dates
  4. What a good outcome looks like to you

Sending us information before an engagement letter is signed does not make you a client.

title: How we bill, in plain English
summary: Hourly, flat and blended fees, monthly invoices, and when we ask for a retainer.
body: Every engagement letter names the fee model, the people who will work on the matter, their rates and the budget by phase. Invoices arrive monthly by email with time entries in plain language. There is no online payment on this site.

title: What to do if you are served with a lawsuit
summary: Note the date, keep everything, and call before the answer deadline.
body:
1. Write down the date and how you were served
  2. Do not contact the other side
  3. Keep every related document and message
  4. Send us the papers the same day

title: Litigation hold notice (template)
summary: A plain-language hold notice to send to employees and vendors, with instructions.
body:
To: [Names]
Re: Keep documents about [matter]

Please keep all documents, email, chat messages and files about [subject] from [date] forward. Do not delete, edit or move them. This applies until you hear from [name] in writing.

Send a copy of every acknowledgment to your matter team.

title: Deposition preparation guide
summary: What a deposition is, how long it takes, and the six rules we will practice together.
body:
1. Listen to the whole question
  2. Pause before you answer
  3. Answer only the question asked
  4. It is fine to say you do not remember
  5. Do not guess at numbers or dates
  6. Ask for a break when you need one (not while a question is pending)

We schedule two preparation sessions before every deposition.

title: Reading your monthly invoice
summary: Phases, time entries, the budget bar and how to ask about a charge.
body: Each invoice shows time by phase against the budget in your engagement letter, with a bar showing what is left. Questions go to your matter partner, never to accounts.

title: Estate plan signing day checklist
summary: What to bring to the signing meeting at the Mill District office.
body:
1. Photo ID
  2. Final drafts you have reviewed
  3. Names and addresses of your agents and trustees
  4. Deeds or account statements for trust funding

title: Board minutes: a model set
summary: Annual meeting, written consent and special committee minutes, with notes on what to leave out.
body: Model minutes record decisions and the information the board relied on, not the debate. Notes in the margin explain each line.
